specificationName: Instance Invariant Storage for Impulses and Activities

evidence: Activity.load implements backend fallback (activity.ts:495-547)
impulse_create syncs to backend via metabob_impulse_store (impulse-create.ts:86-93)
Backend storage indexed by (api_key, project_id) enables cross-instance retrieval
Local cache properly invalidatable - backend is authoritative
All impulse operations: opencode → CLI MCP → rpc-api → SurrealDB
All activity operations: opencode → CLI MCP → rpc-api → SurrealDB
MCP tools act as middleware (metabob-cli/mcp/tools.py)
REST endpoints validate and route (metabob-rpc-api/server/routes/)
No direct database access from opencode
Activity.save writes local + backend sync (activity.ts:674-700)
impulse_create writes SessionMemory + backend sync (impulse-create.ts:86-93)
Activity.load falls back to backend if local missing (activity.ts:495-547)
Backend sync is best-effort but always attempted
Local storage treated as performance cache only
MCP tools extract api_key from config (tools.py)
REST endpoints validate X-API-Key header (impulse.py, activity.py routes)
DB operations enforce WHERE api_key = $api_key (impulse_data.py, activity_data.py)
Composite keys prevent cross-tenant leakage: (api_key, project_id, impulse_id)
All 4 layers enforce isolation: opencode → CLI → API → DB
Activities stored with full metadata in backend
Any instance can retrieve activity via metabob_activity_load
Session state, task results, and metrics persisted centrally
Error traces and validation results accessible cross-instance
Activity templates stored in backend registry
Template changes propagate to all instances instantly
Success rates and metrics shared across instances
No local-only template storage

vesselHierarchy.compliance: All layers correctly implemented and respect hierarchy

testScenarios.verificationPath: Create impulse on Instance A → Query from Instance B → Should retrieve successfully
Save activity on Instance A → Load from Instance B (no local cache) → Should fallback to backend and succeed
Tenant A creates impulse 'shared-name' → Tenant B creates impulse 'shared-name' → Both retrieve only their own

recommendations.recommendation: Add metrics for backend sync success rates to detect MCP connectivity issues early
recommendations.rationale: Backend sync is best-effort; monitoring would improve observability

recommendations.recommendation: Add integration tests for cross-instance scenarios using docker-compose with multiple opencode containers
recommendations.rationale: Current implementation is correct but lacks explicit cross-instance test coverage

recommendations.recommendation: Document the write-through cache pattern in architecture docs
recommendations.rationale: Pattern is implemented correctly but not explicitly documented for new developers

summary: The Instance Invariant Storage specification is FULLY COMPLIANT across all 12 analyzed components spanning 4 repositories. All impulse and activity data correctly flows through the vessel hierarchy (opencode → CLI MCP → rpc-api → SurrealDB) with proper (api_key, project_id) scoping at every layer. Local storage is correctly used only as a performance cache, with the backend serving as the authoritative source. Cross-instance access works via backend fallback mechanisms. Multi-tenant isolation is enforced at all 4 architectural layers. No code changes required.
